options: Lists which servers may send mail for your domain
Signs every message with a private key
Tells receivers to send you reports
questions.why: SPF is a published list of approved sending servers. Signing is DKIM and reporting is DMARC.

questions.q: Why is a forgotten sender the main risk when enforcing DMARC?
options: Its mail would be quarantined or refused
It makes your SPF record shorter
questions.why: Once the policy is quarantine or reject, a legitimate service that fails the checks has its messages sent to spam or refused.

questions.q: How many SPF records may a domain have?
questions.why: Two SPF records is an error and both can fail. Merge services into one record.

questions.q: What happens when an SPF record needs more than 10 DNS lookups?
options: Nothing, the limit is only advice
The record returns an error and may fail
questions.why: Going past 10 lookups causes an SPF error. Remove unused includes and keep the record tidy.

questions.q: Which mechanisms do NOT count towards the lookup limit?
questions.why: Plain ip4 and ip6 entries need no DNS lookup, so they do not count.

questions.q: Where is a DKIM public key published?
options: At the root of your website
questions.why: The selector is a label that forms part of the DNS name, which is why you need it to look a key up.

options: Either SPF or DKIM passing and aligned
questions.why: DMARC needs at least one of SPF or DKIM to pass and align with the visible from domain.

questions.q: Which starting DMARC policy is safe for real mail?
questions.why: p=none only monitors, so no mail is blocked, and the rua address sends you the reports you need.

questions.q: What does the rua tag set?
options: The address that receives aggregate reports
The percentage of mail to block
questions.why: rua is the reporting address. sp sets subdomain policy and pct sets the percentage.

questions.q: Why does forwarding often cause SPF failures?
options: The forwarding server is not in the original sender's SPF list
questions.why: The forwarding server sends the message on, but your SPF does not list it. DKIM usually survives, which is why it matters.

questions.q: What is the sp tag for?
options: Setting a separate DMARC policy for subdomains
questions.why: sp= lets subdomains have their own policy, different from the main domain's p= value.

questions.q: What is the best treatment for a domain you own that never sends email?
options: Point it at your main mailbox
questions.why: A non-sending domain has nothing to break, so lock it down fully so no one can fake it.
